Here is a simple example of how you can write a Semgrep rule for the vulnerable behavior:

```yaml
---
id: CVE-2026-28211
title: NVDA Unsafe Evaluation of Logged Speech Sequence
description: |
  This rule detects when NVDA is evaluating a logged speech sequence using Python's eval() function.
  This can lead to arbitrary code execution if an attacker can manipulate the log data.
severity: WARNING
language: python
metadata:
  tags:
    - security
    - nvda
  version: >=2024.1
---

# This is a YAML comment, it will not be included in the rule.
# The next line is the start of the rule definition.
{
  "name": "unsafe-eval",
  "pattern": "[\\s]*eval\\([\"']?[a-zA-Z0-9_]+[\"']?\\)",
  "taint-mode": "all"
}
```

This rule will match any line that contains the `eval()` function, which is used to evaluate a string as Python code. The pattern `[\\s]*eval\\([\"']?[a-zA-Z0-9_]+[\"']?\\)` matches any line containing `eval()`, where the argument can be an identifier (like a variable name) or a quoted string.

The taint-mode: "all" means that this rule will apply to all files, not just those in the repository.

Please note that this is a very basic example and might need adjustments depending on your specific use case.
